test_title: SSC MTS 2024 Official Paper (Held On: 05 Nov, 2024 Shift 2)
subject: general
question:
Select the word segment that substitutes the bracketed word segment correctly and completes the sentence meaningfully.

The movie was (mostly over) when we entered the hall.
solution:
The correct answer is **Option 2**.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The phrase "**almost over**" is the correct and natural expression used to indicate that something is nearly finished.
 
• The sentence talks about entering the hall when the movie was nearly finished, so "almost over" appropriately conveys that meaning.
 
• Other options are grammatically or contextually incorrect: 
 
 
• **Most done** – awkward and not a standard phrase.
 
• **More done** – comparative, but doesn’t fit the context.
 
• **Most over** – incorrect usage; not idiomatic or grammatically correct.
 
 

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 2**.

 

**Correct Sentence:** *"The movie was **almost over** when we entered the hall."*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• "**Almost over**" is a commonly used phrase in English to show something is nearing its end.
 
• It is often used with time-bound events like shows, meetings, or tasks (e.g., "The class was almost over").
